source_caption:
Trading 7 years for 86 years. 

The series finale of Better Call Saul delivered what is arguably the most unspoken, heartbreaking farewell in television history. Jimmy McGill had the ultimate victory in his hands. Using his ruthless legal mind, he took a lifetime sentence for his crimes in Breaking Bad and argued it down to a ridiculous 7.5 years in a comfortable prison. He had won the game. But he realized that winning meant losing Kim Wexler forever so he confesses to everything not to save himself, but to protect Kim and finally regain his soul. He trades a 7-year freedom ticket for 86 years behind bars. 

When Kim visits him one last time and leaves the prison, there are no tears. He shoots her his signature finger guns a tragic, quiet acknowledgment that while Saul Goodman is gone, Jimmy McGill finally came back.

source_details.synopsis: Better Call Saul is an American neo-noir legal crime drama television series created by Vince Gilligan and Peter Gould for AMC. Part of the Breaking Bad franchise, it is a spin-off of Gilligan's previous series, Breaking Bad (2008–2013), to which it serves primarily as a prequel, with some scenes taking place during and after the events of Breaking Bad. Better Call Saul premiered on AMC on February 8, 2015, and ended on August 15, 2022, after six seasons, totaling 63 episodes.
